findings.title: Unchecked destructure of window.__workbenchTemplateGating silently kills entire IIFE on load failure
findings.why_it_matters: If workbench-template-gating.js fails to load for any reason (404, CDN error, caching race during a deploy, CSP block), window.__workbenchTemplateGating is undefined. The bare destructure `const { ... } = window.__workbenchTemplateGating` throws a synchronous TypeError inside the IIFE. Because the IIFE has no outer try/catch, execution halts at line 6996 and nothing below that line runs: all event handlers, DOMContentLoaded wiring, state init, and UI binding are all skipped. The workbench renders its HTML shell but is completely non-functional, with no user-visible error message. The window.onerror / unhandledrejection recorder wired at line 331 does fire — but only if the IIFE got that far; since the crash is at line 6996 of ~8688, the recorder is already installed and will capture it. However there is no recovery path and the user sees a frozen UI with no explanation.
findings.suggested_fix:
Add a null-guard before the destructure: `const _gating = window.__workbenchTemplateGating; if (!_gating) { document.body.innerHTML = '

Fatal: workbench-template-gating.js failed to load. Please reload.

'; return; }` then destructure `_gating`. Alternatively, provide inline fallback constants so a missing file degrades gracefully rather than crashing: `const _gating = window.__workbenchTemplateGating || {}; const BUNDLE_ACTION_ORDER = _gating.BUNDLE_ACTION_ORDER || ['idle','attack','death']; ...`. No new dependencies needed — this is a handful of lines.
evidence: web/workbench.js line 6996: `const { BUNDLE_ACTION_ORDER, isTemplateActionAuthorable: _isTemplateActionAuthorable, getEnabledActions: _getEnabledActions } = window.__workbenchTemplateGating;` — no null check, bare destructure of potentially-undefined global
web/workbench.js line 1: IIFE `(() => { ... })()` has no enclosing try/catch; a synchronous throw anywhere inside kills all subsequent code in the file
web/workbench.html lines 538-540: three synchronous classic scripts; load order is guaranteed but network failure for the first script leaves the global unset
web/workbench-template-gating.js line 98: assignment `window.__workbenchTemplateGating = { ... }` only executes if the file loads and parses successfully

findings.title: No error boundary or user-visible message when the IIFE crashes mid-execution
findings.why_it_matters: Any uncaught synchronous throw inside the IIFE (including the one above but also any future regression) leaves the DOM fully rendered but completely inert. There is no fallback message, no retry affordance, and no visible indication to the user that JS failed. The window.error recorder at line 331 captures the event in memory, but only the bug-report modal (which itself requires JS) can surface it. A user encountering this sees a page that looks loaded but does not respond.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the IIFE body in a top-level try/catch that, on failure, renders a minimal error banner directly into document.body and re-throws (so window.onerror still fires): `try { ... all existing code ... } catch (err) { const b = document.createElement('div'); b.style.cssText='position:fixed;top:0;left:0;right:0;padding:12px;background:#c00;color:#fff;z-index:9999;font:14px monospace'; b.textContent='Workbench failed to start: ' + err.message; document.body.prepend(b); throw err; }`. This is about 6 lines and requires no libraries.
evidence: web/workbench.js line 1-2: `(() => { 'use strict';` — IIFE with no catch
web/workbench.js line 8688: `})();` — IIFE closes without any outer error handler

web/workbench.js lines 331-344: window.error and unhandledrejection handlers are installed inside the IIFE itself, so a crash before line 306 (installUiRecorderHooks, called at line 8557) would not even have the recorder wired; a crash at line 6996 is after the recorder is wired but there is still no user-visible recovery

findings.title: MutationObserver installed by UI recorder is never disconnected
findings.why_it_matters: installUiRecorderHooks (called unconditionally at line 8557, and again on startUiRecorder) creates a MutationObserver that observes several DOM nodes for the lifetime of the page. The observer is stored at state.uiRecorder.statusObserver but is never disconnected — not in stopUiRecorder, not in clearUiRecorder, not in beforeunload. For a single-page session this is benign, but if the workbench is embedded, hot-reloaded, or mounted/unmounted (e.g., in the future Turbo or iframe-swap scenario), the observer keeps a live reference to the old DOM nodes and its callback keeps firing against a stale closure. The installed guard prevents duplicate observers on the same page load, but does not help across reloads.
findings.suggested_fix: In the beforeunload handler block (around line 8139) add `if (state.uiRecorder.statusObserver) { state.uiRecorder.statusObserver.disconnect(); }`. If the workbench is ever embedded or hot-reloaded, also call disconnect in whatever teardown path replaces the page. No library needed.
evidence: web/workbench.js lines 346-356: MutationObserver created and stored in state.uiRecorder.statusObserver, no disconnect path exists anywhere in the file
web/workbench.js line 379-386: clearUiRecorder resets events/seq/active but does not call observer.disconnect()
web/workbench.js line 371-377: stopUiRecorder sets active=false but does not disconnect observer
web/workbench.js lines 8139-8140: beforeunload handlers present for readyPoll and termpp stream, but not for the MutationObserver

findings.title: openWebbuild/reloadWebbuild race: overwritten readyPoll interval without guaranteed prior clearance
findings.why_it_matters: Both openWebbuild (line 1007) and reloadWebbuild (line 1026) call stopWebbuildReadyPoll() then immediately start a new interval and write the handle to state.webbuild.readyPoll. If two rapid calls to either function occur before the first detectWebbuildReady tick executes (e.g., user double-clicks Test This Skin, or a programmatic call races with a load event), the first interval handle is cleared correctly because stopWebbuildReadyPoll is called — so no duplicate poll. However, the `setTimeout(() => { frame.src = nextSrc; }, 10)` at line 1004/1023 is not guarded: if a second call arrives within 10ms, two deferred src assignments race. The second assignment wins on src, but the first deferred callback still fires and may overwrite it back to the stale URL. This is a narrow but real window (10ms).
findings.suggested_fix: Track the deferred src timeout handle: `state.webbuild.srcTimer = setTimeout(...)` and call `clearTimeout(state.webbuild.srcTimer)` at the top of openWebbuild/reloadWebbuild alongside stopWebbuildReadyPoll. Initialise state.webbuild.srcTimer: null alongside readyPoll. No library needed — this is two lines of state init and two clearTimeout calls.
evidence: web/workbench.js line 1004: `setTimeout(() => { try { frame.src = nextSrc; } catch (_e) {} }, 10);` — deferred, untracked handle
web/workbench.js line 1023: same pattern in reloadWebbuild
web/workbench.js line 163: state.webbuild.readyPoll tracked and cleared, but no equivalent for the src assignment timeout

residual_risks: Script load order is guaranteed for synchronous classic scripts in the same HTML document, but a Service Worker or aggressive cache policy that serves workbench.html from cache while workbench-template-gating.js gets a network 404 could break the invariant without any code change.

The dual-export pattern in workbench-template-gating.js (CommonJS vs browser global) means a bundler that inlines both files could accidentally omit the window assignment if it tree-shakes the else branch. Worth verifying if a build step is ever added.

The 900ms setTimeout at line 8685 that rebuilds the wbIdOverlay fires unconditionally after IIFE execution. If the page is navigated away from quickly (e.g., Turbo drive), this fires on a dead DOM without error but represents an unguarded timer that could theoretically accumulate across SPA navigations if the workbench is ever embedded in one.
testing_gaps: No test covers the failure path where workbench-template-gating.js returns a non-200 response — the P0 crash is entirely untested.
No test exercises rapid double-invocation of openWebbuild or reloadWebbuild to expose the deferred src-assignment race.
The MutationObserver lifecycle (connect/disconnect) has no coverage in any verifier lane.
